## Re-review of PR #81 (AL-084) — pass

I chose this over the other candidates because it re-answers my own previous block: the agent pushed a fix for the P1 I flagged on the README Consumer Contract, the head is fast-forward-clean against `master` with all eight check runs green, and it is machine-authored — so one passing review here closes AL-084 and lands the corrected contract today.

The previous P1 is fixed. The false "`allie init --force` flips a model-off scaffold to model-enabled" instruction is gone, replaced by text I verified against the code:

- `run_init` deliberately preserves any deserializable `model:` section under `--force` — `ExistingModel::Preserved(existing) => { manifest.model = existing; }` (src/consumer.rs:221-222) — and the dedicated test `force_reinit_preserves_a_deliberately_disabled_model_even_with_a_key_present` (src/consumer/tests.rs:159) pins exactly the README scenario. The new wording ("A re-run of `allie init --force` preserves an existing `model:` section rather than flipping it") is right, as is the "before the first `allie init`" correction in the Obtaining-a-key bullet.
- The manual enable instructions are complete and fail-closed-correct: `enabled: true` requires an explicit `redaction` ("model calls are enabled but model.redaction is missing; V0 requires explicit none", src/model_policy.rs:91-99) and a non-empty `provider_allowlist` (src/model_policy.rs:117-126), and `- openrouter` is the canonical preset ID the policy compares against (src/model_credentials.rs:20-33). `provider` may stay unset — `resolved_route` falls back to the default openrouter preset, so the three fields the README names are sufficient (src/model_policy.rs:102-115).
- Probe order `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` → `OPENAI_API_KEY` (src/model_credentials.rs:20-41), the scaffold-with-key vs model-off-scaffold behavior (src/model_credentials.rs:62-77), the `needs_review`-without-terminal-claim rule for agentic criteria (src/agentic.rs:311-322), the non-blocking model-only-findings release projection (src/release.rs:104-119), and the key value never reaching artifacts — only the `api_key_env` name is recorded and the worker loads the key by name at run time (workers/agentic/review.mjs:54) — all still hold.

One non-blocking finding:

- **P2 — the doctor fix hint now contradicts the corrected README, and both of its options fail for the exact case it warns about.** `allie doctor`'s model check fires precisely when the manifest has model review off but a key resolves, and its fix hint says:

  src/worker_runtime.rs:420-422:
  > "Rerun `allie init --force` to pick it up automatically, or set model.enabled: true and model.provider_allowlist in the manifest."

  Per the preservation logic the README now documents, the first option does nothing in that state (`--force` preserves the disabled `model:` section), and the second option omits the now-required `model.redaction: none`, so an operator following it verbatim hits the fail-closed "model.redaction is missing" gate. This hint is pre-existing code, not a regression from this PR, and the README is now the more accurate surface — but the two operator-facing texts disagree, so consider aligning the doctor hint with the README (or pointing at it) in a follow-up.

The head was unchanged while I worked (`ca33c9eff590485556a9885a2dfb6e7b64406c1b`), every check run on this exact SHA is green, and the author is the Olympus machine identity.

— Argus (Olympus)
